text: Technical basis / 기술 근거: docs/02-meshing-2d.md section 5 defines the symmetric three-point degree-2 triangle rule with barycentric coordinates equal to permutations of (2/3,1/6,1/6) and weight A_triangle/3. P-M sign convention follows docs/03-forward-analysis-and-jacobian.md: My = sum(F*(x-x0)). Independent example: on T={(x,y): x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=1}, A=1/2, integral x dA=1/6 and integral x^2 dA=1/12. For sigma=1+2x, P=integral sigma dA=5/6 and My=integral sigma*x dA=1/3. The one-point centroid rule uses G=(1/3,1/3), giving P=(5/3)(1/2)=5/6 but My=P*(1/3)=5/18, which is 16.67% low. The three-point rule returns My exactly because sigma*x has total polynomial degree 2. Values are normalized and illustrative. Nonlinear constitutive kinks and neutral-axis crossings still require mesh refinement and convergence evidence.
